This book was probably written around the time of Hush House's Baronial Period - roughly 1500s to 1700s. If I examine it, I can learn more about what knowledge it might contain. [Books from this period are only rarely contaminated.]

This book was probably written around the time of Hush House's Curia Period - roughly 1700s to 1800s. If I examine it, I can learn more about what knowledge it might contain. [Books from this period are only rarely contaminated.]

This book was probably written around the time of Hush House's Dawn Period - some time before the end of the first millennium, commonly reckoned. If I examine it, I can learn more about what knowledge it might contain. [Books from this period are sometimes contaminated.]

This book was probably written around the time of Hush House's Nocturnal Period - after the turn of the century. If I examine it, I can learn more about what knowledge it might contain. [Books from this period are almost never contaminated.]

This book was probably written around the time of Hush House's Solar Gothic Period - roughly, between the 1000s and the 1500s. If I examine it, I can learn more about what knowledge it might contain. [Books from this period are occasionally contaminated.]
Trist is already half a hand trailed in a river of deeper sadness. [A defeat when Edge is present can submerge trist in despair.]
Uneven symbols in a complex pattern, veering off in all directions. The shapes are heavy with half-felt meaning... but I can't read it.

When the Librarian of Hush House determines their answer to one of the great mysteries... the Hours themselves might pay attention.

[Making a Determination is the first step towards writing your own History. It will require no less than 20 of a Power aspect. This means suitably potent Soul, Memory, and Skill, as well as a carefully chosen ink.]

[To record a new History, you'll need an ink of power; one of the great secrets known as Numina, which usually dwell in the most hallowed books; and 25 points of a Power aspect. This is easier if you've made at least one, and preferably two, suitable Determinations.]

Five notables are ready to establish the Lighthouse Institute, the successor to the Curia of the Isle. Since no replacement is available for Rowena, she will continue as Secretary Persistent. Perhaps this is evidence to support Clogg's Law: 'Over time, an occult organisation will prove increasingly unable to rid itself of its immortal members.' [Once you've taken this step, you'll no longer be able to change your preferences for candidates - and if any candidates die or disappear, the Lighthouse Institute will be stillborn. If you've selected candidates with opposing Agendas, Fears or Sympathies, those inspirations will be deadlocked.]
For some reason, not everyone can attend. Travelling? Lost? If I repeat the agreed signal, will it work this time?
From across the Wake they come, by land and sea and sky, like birds at sunset...
I'll need six suitable candidates - enough to reconstitute the old structure of the Curia of the Isle, with a new Secretary Persistent to replace Rowena.

The founders of the Lighthouse Institute have returned to Brancrug. [To continue, place your journal in a Hush House room with all six founders.]

These are the six founders; they are almost ready to inaugurate their Institute. The seventh, unacknowledged, is the Librarian. [To continue, place your journal in a Hush House room with all six founders. Place your journal in the Lighthouse to summon them quickly.]

This is not a step to take lightly. I should convene the Institute only when I'm ready to host a meeting that makes the final decisions: including appropriate tea and cake, or suitable alternatives. [The founders will come to Hush House unless they're travelling home or otherwise unavailable.]
Investigate insight from an incident. [This will give you a Persistent Memory. Alternatively, combine two Inklings if you'd like to try something unwise.]
It is not the Librarian's business to meddle in the world beyond Hush House. But sometimes the Librarian gets curious. [This will create an Avenue of Enquiry.]

It is not the Librarian's business to meddle in the world beyond Hush House. But sometimes the Librarian gets curious; sometimes the Librarian misuses their prerogatives because they grow restless. [This will precipitate an Incident, if any yet remain undrawn. If there's already an Incident, Visitors might not initially interact with the one you intend. Instigate informedly, Ys-incipient.]
[No Incident has occurred, this time. Perhaps some kind of ending approaches. We might even say immanesces, if we were those sort of people.]

One founder insisted we should ally with Ys; another refused, warning of Ys' legendary and fundamental treachery.
One founder insisted we should ally with the Chandler; another was horrified at any dealings with that rising power.
One founder insisted we should embrace our kinship with the Carapace Cross; another refused to countenance any loss of our truer humanity.
The Institute has resolved that Ys, the city beyond the wave, has been left unchallenged too long: its seductions might capsize the waking world.
The Institute has resolved that the all-consuming horror of the gods-from-Nowhere is the greatest threat mortalkind ever need fear.
The Institute has resolved that the benefits of working with Ys greatly outweigh its dangers.
The Institute has resolved that the coming Hour called Chandler is the most serious occult threat to mortalkind.
The Institute has resolved that the returning Carapace Cross, and the changes that might come, are the most significant occult threat to mortalkind.
The Institute has resolved to forge alliances with the Carapace Cross, as their return begins.
The Institute has resolved to guard mortalkind first against the perils of the hidden world: alukites, Mansus-spirits, hungry ghosts...
The Institute has resolved to make a mutually beneficial arrangement with the merchants of years.
The institute has resolved to work with the Chandler... when the Chandler finally becomes manifest.
[Deadlock: founders have opposing Fear/Sympathy. We can't inaugurate the Institute with Ys as either an Ally or a Foe]
[Deadlock: founders have opposing Fear/Sympathy. We can't inaugurate the Institute with the Carapace Cross as either an Ally or a Foe.]

After hours of argument, we were unable to settle to a specific mission, beyond 'to keep all mortalkind from the rocks of eternal night.'
One founder argued for the benefits of conflict. Another insisted on its futility...
One founder argued that Calyptra protected us - another, that it burdened us intolerably...
One founder argued that we should honour the gods of the redder sun - another, that they were both a danger and a resource to be consumed...
Ready for the Institute's Inaugural Meeting?
The Institute will unrearth, preserve, honour, recall something of the gods-from-stone, who came before the Hours we know.
[Deadlock: founders have opposing Agendas. We can't inaugurate the Institute with  Mission: Stone Remembered or Consumed.]

In this part of the world, we picnic only in Spring and Summer.
Make sure there's at least one thing in the room for every visitor to eat.
Make sure there's one thing in the room for every visitor to drink.
One does not picnic when it's too dark to apply jam without peril of jam-related accidents.
One might only have Elevenses in the morning; and Afternoon Tea only at the appropriate time for afternoon tea.
One might only have Lunch or Supper after midday.
One really shouldn't serve Intoxicating drinks with Elevenses or with Afternoon Tea.
Perhaps someone has tried to hold a Salon in Numa at some point. Perhaps at several points. We'll never know, because no records of an attempt have survived. [No Salons in Numa.]
Raw meat and vegetables might be suitable as gifts to assistants, but not as meals for guests. Make sure there's nothing Raw in the room.
Visitors marked as Unsociable are wary of other Visitors. They won't attend the usual kind of Salon - although they will attend a final Salon to inaugurate the Institute.

[Salons here must be in Morning or Afternoon, with at least two guests. The more guests, the more successful, but you'll need enough food and drink in the room for everyone - and since this will be Elevenses or Afternoon Tea, nothing Intoxicating.]
